prediction_question: For a reported wildlife strike to a civil aircraft, will the strike result in damage to the aircraft?
prediction_time: The circumstances of the strike as recorded on the FAA strike report (form 5200-7): airport, state, FAA region, aircraft make/mass, phase of flight, height, speed, visibility, precipitation, species. Damage fields and per-part damage flags are the outcome and are excluded from features.
target_definition: Binary: aircraft damage (damage level in {M, M?, S, D} on the published scale, or any damage flag) recorded in the strike report.

third_party_published_figures_2026_10_19.source: arXiv 2608.12390 (open versioned aggregates of the NWSD)
third_party_published_figures_2026_10_19.observed: frozen seed of 347,575 strike reports spanning incident years 1990-2026 (4,010 in partial 2026); damaging defined as DAMAGE_LEVEL in {M, M?, S, D}; commercial subset AC_MASS in {3,4,5}

174,104 records, 65 original columns, target 'Aircraft Damage' with class balance 91.4% no-damage / 8.6% damage; post-strike leakage columns identified and dropped; tuned random forest reaches 62% damage recall from pre-strike features only

measurements.note: None of these figures were measured by this session; they are third-party published measurements of the same source, labelled as such. No probe was run because the novelty rejection came first.

rejection_reason: Equivalent already exists in usable form, so per the standing novelty test this is a rejection, not a candidate. The exact task - predict aircraft damage from pre-strike information only - is public, de-risked and even leakage-audited by third parties: (1) github.com/oldguy773/FAA-Wildlife-Strike-analysis ships a full pipeline on the public database.csv with the post-strike damage-flag leakage identified, fixed and documented, plus feature importances (aircraft mass, species, phase of flight, visibility, height, speed); (2) Misra et al. 2022 (Int J Sustainable Aviation 10.1504/IJSA.2022.122328) trains RF/ANN/logreg/SVM/XGBoost/KNN on the same database with random forest at 78.81% accuracy and the same top variables (bird size, impact height, airspeed, aircraft mass); (3) a 2025 helicopter-specific study (2013-2022, 2,816 strikes, 14.38% damaging) does the same task for a segment; (4) arXiv 2608.12390 publishes open versioned aggregates of the same database by family/airframe/airport for 1990-2026. What exists: the source, the task, the pre-strike feature discipline, the leakage findings and the headline accuracies. What would be ours: only splits and packaging - a mirror, not a contribution. The one thing none of them ship is a scored runner contract, which does not clear the operator's bar ('a source whose equivalent already exists in a usable form is a rejection').
next_action: None - dropped on novelty (2026-10-19). Do not reopen for damage prediction from pre-strike strike-report fields. A re-open would need a materially different task on this source (e.g. something about construction quality rather than the prediction itself), which would be a new candidate with its own novelty search.
